Child Brides

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As South Africans we think the tragedy of child brides only exists outside our borders, but in fact there are over 90 000 girls being forced into marriage right here, many as young as 14.

Summary:
Pamela was 16 when her sister forced her into marrying a much older man, as the family were struggling financially. She was removed from school and taken to the mans village to live as his wife.
“I was so sad because I was a clever girl and I wanted to become a teacher” Pamela
He beat her violently throughout their marriage. She lived as this mans wife until she escaped at 30, they have three children together. Pamela is now 32 and lives in a new village where she works with the Dutwya women's group, speaking to families about the importance of sending their girl children to school and the damage that forcing early marriage does to a child

Zanele (not her real name) was 14 when her mom forced her to marry a man from a neighbouring village. The man is a 26 year old mine worker who works in JHB.
She was taken to the village and forced to live in a house with this man and his mother. She escaped and swam across the Mbashe river to get home. Once she got back to her house her mother simply reprimanded her for not doing her duty for the family and took her back to the mans house, where she sat on the couch in the lounge and didn’t sleep for 4 days. She knew that if she fell asleep or went to the bedroom she would be raped. She was rescued by the hawks and Mr Majola (Khula development Project).

The man and his mother have been prosecuted with Abduction and trafficking, no sentence yet. I have to find out more about what happened to her mother, waiting for Kerry from the Commission for Gender Equality to come back to SA on Saturday. Obviously she has been removed from her home and has been placed in a place of safety.
Incident took place December 2017, so she is okay to speak about it anonymously




Further information:
According to Mr Majola and Vuvu (Head of Dutwya Women's support group) with all these cases in the Eastern Cape the families explain to them that Ukuthwala is part of their culture and they have the right to marry off their children.
This is why the CGE are fighting for the practice of Ukuthwala to become a criminal offence.
Sorry I don't think I explained this well in the pitch..

Script:










Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Voice over When a child’s mother, the one person she trusts, forces her into marriage
who does she have to turn to for help, how does she escape?
2 00:11 Zandi My mother turned me away and said I must be married off. I was crying and I didn’t want to go.
3 00:20 Masa link As I stand here over 90 000 young girls many as young 14 are living as child brides across South Africa. Girls who had their whole lives ahead of them, we investigate the child bride crisis specifically here in the Eastern Cape.
4 00:37 Voice over Kerry Oosthuysen is the provincial legal officer for the commission for gender
equality in the Eastern Cape she works closely with the community and the
courts with regards to forced child marriages, which are often mistakenly
referred to as Ukuthwala.
5 00:51 Kerry interview with Masa Kerry: Ukutwala was a customary practice where it was used as means to force lobola negotiations. So it was an abduction of a young girl by a person of the same age which would then force the family to negotiate marriage. There was consent on both parties, there was no forced sexual intercourse at any stage. Currently we are seeing a polluted version of ukutwala. The Commissions view is that ukutwala its in polluted sense is a criminal act because there is no consent of the young child and also at what age can you give that consent it’s a guise for human traffic and forced marriage
6 01:31 Masa link Zandi which is not her real name to protect her identity, was allegedly forced into marriage by her mother. She was sold to a man who was 12 years older than her. Taken to the man’s house under the guise of helping her grandmother collect money and then locked in a tiny room
7 01:48 Zandi
The man arrives and asks me to marry him, I refuse and cry. The mother of the house arrives saying she is going to buy me things to wear to be the wife. Then the man says I must come sleep and I refuse and sit on the stool. I was thinking about the fact that they might rape me or do anything to me.
8 02:12 Voice over Zandi sat on the same chair for three days refusing to eat or sleep.

Petrus Majola is the director of Khula a community development project
specifically focusing on the Rural Eastern Cape, together with the Hawks he
was directly involved in Rescuing Zandi after receiving a tip off from the local
community that a young girl was being held against her will
9 02:25 Majola and Masa interview Majola: At the time, we arrived in the area the girl managed already to escape and apparently, she escaped going home crossing the river but on arrival at home she was sent back by her biological mother and then she escaped again. So, we went straight to where the mother resides and that’s how we got hold of the girl.
10 03:00 Voice over Captain Jack is the Hawks investigating officer for human trafficking cases in the
Eastern Cape, she worked closely with Majola on Zandi’s case
11 03:07 Captain Jack And I drove Mr Majola to that homestead and we rescued the child. We take the child and put her in a safe space and social development was in place. It’s very hard to find these cases because the perpetrators are the parents. If the child didn’t have chance to escape we would not know that the child has gone through ukutwala.
12 03:32 Masa Link Pamela was 126 when she was abducted for a 33-year-old man and forced to live as his wife

13 03:39 Pamela and Masa interview Pamela: We were walking and all of a sudden, I’m being grabbed, one holds my one hand and the other holds my other hand and I start crying. I’m crying along the way and screaming and screaming and I’m thinking maybe they are twala-ing me. Then we arrive at the house and I sit and wait to find out who it is that I am being brought to. Maybe after 30 minutes a lady says “why are you crying? these things you see here are going to be your, you will have money and you won’t suffer again” I even tried to leave through the window but they caught me while I was trying to escape. They brought me back and this man came and said “you are going to be my wife, so please come sleep in the bed” and I said I don’t want to. I sit and I continue crying, I’m not making noise, tears are just rolling down my face.
14 04:38 Masa link For almost 2 years Pamela’s family didn’t know where she was until her abductors family returned to pay lobola
15 04:47 Voice over Lobola or the payment of money for a bride is seen as a motivating factor behind forced child marriages in the Eastern Cape and across South Africa.
16 04:55 Majola Majola: Poverty is always sighted as one of the contributing factors. In another area of Baziya they were talking about 7 cows and R6000. But you look at 7 cows and R6000 and you compare that to the value of the child.
16 05:17 Kerry Kerry: There is a belief that there is a close link between poverty and Ukutwala specifically where it is promised that your daughter will have a better life.

17 05:28 Voice over Currently there is no specific law prohibiting Ukuthwala or forced child marriages, so the NPA is forced to use various existing laws to prosecute these cases.
18 05:38 Kerry The main one for us is the trafficking persons act. There is a specific section which prohibits forced marriages and the trafficking of children for sexual purposes.
19 05:49 Voice over Zandi’s mom and everyone who was involved in her being forced into marriage have been charged with contravening the trafficking persons act. The trial is scheduled for July
20 05:58 Zandi I don’t know why my mother wanted to marry me off. I don’t know what had gotten into her. I miss her because she is my mother and she asked for forgiveness and I accepted it because she’s my mother
21 06:13 Voice over Pamela never managed to escape and she was never rescued. After being married for two years she had her first child and her nightmare continued for 13 more years.
22 06:24 Masa and Pamela Masa: How was it in your marriage?
Pamela: It was ugly and painful. He would hold me by my collar and he would push me around and push me to the wall. He beat me at night, if he wanted to sleep with me he would pin me down and I would cry and he would say “I will do it even though you don’t want to”. I feel like my life… my husband made it difficult for me
23 07:05 Voice over One night enough was enough and Pamela packed everything she had and escaped with her three children. That was two years ago. Today she is free and putting her life back together. She travels amongst the neighbouring villages telling other women her story and speaking out against forced child marriages
24 07:27 Masa and Kerry Masa: When we talk about the communities where this is happening, do they see as this? do they see it as the natural and traditional form of ukutwala or are they seeing it as it is?

Kerry: Through our community engagement, there have been different views. In some instances, there is a firm resolve that ukutwala is a customary practice and should be practiced whilst in other communities there is a strong view that it won’t be tolerated and in all forms, it would be reported to SAPS and the relevant traditional leader.

25 07:58 Officer Jack In the rural areas of the Eastern Cape the kids are not safe. Within our environment the SAPS we don’t have much man power so we cannot be in house by house to make sure the kids have not gone ukutwala but we are trying our level best to make sure that whenever a case comes to our attention we attend to it quickly so that the child could be rescued immediately.
26 08:23 Voice over Even though there are still a large number of children being forced into marriage across South Africa there is potential for a new law reform that will make saving these children and getting the perpetrators prosecuted a lot easier.
27 08:38 Kerry and Masa Kerry: The South African law form commission undertook a project where they investigated and interrogated where there is a need for a specific statue prohibiting ukutwala and other forms of forced child marriage. They released a discussion paper where they included a draft bill. Currently the report is before the minister of justice. We do not have the time frames as to when he would be able to consider the report. It was provided to him mid-year last year. Oi do believe that the successful prosecution of persons involved in ukutwala will send a strong message to communities to say this will not be tolerated. That there are sever consequences for this type of activity because it violates, grossly violates the constitutional rights of young girls.
28 09:29 Voice over Regardless of what happen at her mom’s trail Zandi will indefinitely be living with family outside of the Eastern Cape.
29 09:41 Zandi When I finish school, I want to be a social worker, because I want to help others like me that are in the village. When I think about what happened to me I don’t want other to grow up like that
